rows: In every school, students have time to learn and practice the essential skills for their grade or course. They can explain what they are learning and why it matters, recognize good work, and check their own work while they still have time to improve it.

Support to Take the Next Step
Students use timely support, collaboration, and reflection to keep doing challenging work and identify their next step.
Students recognize their growth, demonstrate mastery, prepare for what comes next, and experience well-being and belonging in their learning community.
Students explain their reasoning, evaluate evidence, or defend a solution at the level the Kentucky Priority Standard requires.
Students learn to reason with evidence and meet the thinking demands of the standard.
B1. A3 supports review of the essential knowledge students use.
Learning in Context and Across Subjects

Students use what they are learning to tackle a meaningful problem, including Kentucky or Fleming County examples where they fit. When a task draws on more than one subject, students explain how those connections helped them address the problem.
Meaningful contexts and connections help students apply their learning.
B3, B4. A1 supports the connection between the purpose of learning and its context.
Students identify a decision their input helped shape and explain what changed in their learning experience.
Student input helps shape learning experiences that matter to them.
Students make a meaningful choice about what they investigate, how they approach the work, or how they show their learning. They explain how that choice helps them meet the learning goal.
Purposeful choice builds ownership while keeping the learning goal clear.
Students pursue curriculum-connected questions tied to their interests, passions, or aspirations, or explain how a skill or talent they chose to use helped them meet the learning goal.
Students connect their strengths and aspirations to meaningful learning.

Students write weekly in every course to develop or communicate their understanding of the subject. They might explain a solution in math, interpret evidence in science, or defend a claim in social studies.
Writing makes students’ thinking and understanding visible.
Compelling Evidence and BRIDGE Performance Assessments

Students produce multiple pieces of evidence for each Kentucky Priority Standard. In scheduled BRIDGE Performance Assessments (BPAs), they apply their learning and explain how their work demonstrates the targeted BRIDGE Performance Indicators (BPIs).
Multiple pieces of evidence show how students apply learning and demonstrate the targeted indicators.
D2, D3, D4. E4 supports review across multiple measures.
BPI Portfolios and Presentations of Learning

In grades 3-12, students select evidence for their BPI portfolios and explain what it shows. During scheduled Presentations of Learning, they use that evidence to describe their progress, what they can do, and what comes next.
Students use their own evidence to explain progress and plan what comes next.
Students show what they understand during instruction. Teachers use that evidence to adjust instruction, provide support, or increase the challenge while students are still learning.
Evidence during learning helps teachers respond while students can still improve.
Students receive specific feedback tied to the learning expectation, have time to use it, and explain what they changed or tried next.
Students need time and clear feedback to improve their work.
E2. B2 supports the finding when students use an example to guide a revision.
When students get stuck, they use a prompt, tool, or strategy to continue doing the grade-level thinking themselves.
Support helps students move forward without removing the challenging thinking.

Students use evidence from earlier and later work to describe how their learning has changed.
Recognizing progress helps students identify strategies and next steps.
Students demonstrate what they know and can do against clear learning expectations.

Students connect their learning and goals to the next grade, course, or opportunity.
Purposeful preparation helps students approach their next step with confidence.
Students describe a sense of belonging and identify people, routines, or strategies that support their well-being.
Students need supportive relationships and a sense of belonging to engage in learning.
